objective: Authentication and authorization: sessions, CSRF, sign-in and register throttles, default-deny RBAC, admin bootstrap (ARCH-25, SEC-1, SEC-9, SEC-20, F-TR-17, RS-30, FU-6, FU-11).
context: Built against spec revision 3 (Authentication ARCH-25, RBAC matrix, Security T4/T6/T7/T8/T24, Rate limiting), the F-TR-17 review finding, followups FU-6 and FU-11, and b1's handoffs (router requires a policy; non-public routes were 401 until an authorize hook exists; seed hash format scrypt$16384$8$1$salt$key). Memory search for auth, throttle, scrypt, session returned nothing; the one lesson shown at claim (guard root resolution) is not about this task.
expectedOutput: Auth routes csrf/register/signin/signout/session, session store, CSRF, throttles, RBAC access hook wired into createApp, admin bootstrap from RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD, audit service, and tests.
acceptanceCriteria: Routes /api/auth/csrf, register, signin, signout, session as specified; cookie rs_sid HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age 43200, Secure on https; only sha256(id) stored; idle 60 min and absolute 12 h; rotation on sign-in and register (any incoming session destroyed, SEC-20); role always customer on register; RS_ALLOW_SIGNUP=0 -> 403 SIGNUP_DISABLED
CSRF: session-bound X-CSRF-Token on every non-GET route, pre-login HMAC token for signin/register, Origin check -> 403 CSRF_FAILED; POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey is exempt

SEC-1/SEC-9 throttle in SQLite: hard 429 at 5 failures per (username_key, IP) or 20 per IP in 15 min before the password check; cross-IP failures only delay (1-10 s), never refuse; username_key = lower(NFC(trim)); unknown usernames counted alike; identical 401 for unknown user and bad password with a dummy scrypt

F-TR-17: register is limited per IP per hour by RS_REGISTER_PER_IP_PER_HOUR (default 5); auth.test.js runs with the default and asserts the 6th registration from one IP -> 429 with details.limit register_ip

RBAC: every route module declares its policy next to each route; startup fails for a route without one; anonymous 401, wrong role 403, admin routes require role admin; admin account created or updated from RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD (>= 16 chars) as scrypt and disabled when unset (SEC-5)
auth.test.js names its cases with ARCH-25, SEC-1, SEC-9, SEC-13, SEC-20 and asserts no Access-Control-Allow-* header on any response
FU-6: password.js verifies the seed hash format and the dummy hash uses the same parameters; a test signs in a seeded account
FU-11: forwarded client IP validated with net.isIP; invalid falls back to the socket address; test named SEC-B-9
completedWork: ROUTES (src/routes/auth.js): GET csrf, POST register, POST signin (public; they run Origin + pre-login-or-session CSRF themselves), POST signout (policy session), GET session (public, uses ctx.auth.identify). Cookie rs_sid=<43 chars>; Path=/; Max-Age=43200; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (+Secure when RS_PUBLIC_URL is https); sign-out sends Max-Age=0. Sessions (src/auth/sessions.js): 32 random bytes, only sha256 stored, idle 60 min (last_seen refreshed at most once a minute, a busy DB on that refresh is ignored), absolute 12 h, disabled users do not resolve, disableUser deletes sessions. Sign-in and register destroy the incoming session in the same transaction that creates the new one (SEC-20); an attacker-planted id is never adopted. CSRF (src/auth/csrf.js): pre-login token nonce.hmac (nonce = 8-byte time + 16 random bytes, HMAC-SHA256 with meta csrf_key, 2 h, small future skew), session token compared in constant time, Origin must equal RS_PUBLIC_URL's origin or http(s)://<Host>. Throttle (src/auth/throttle.js): an attempt is counted when admitted, in the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE as the check (so parallel requests cannot overshoot); pair >=5 -> 429 signin_pair, IP >=20 -> 429 signin_ip, both before the password check; >=10 failures for the username across IPs -> delay min(10,(n-9)) s then the password is still checked; success deletes that pair's rows including its own reservation; unknown usernames take the same path and one scrypt against a dummy hash with the seed's parameters; 401 body is identical for unknown, wrong password and disabled. Register limit uses rate_events kind register, key ip:<addr>, reserved after validation and before hashing. Password (src/auth/password.js): async scrypt N=16384 r=8 p=1 key 64, accepts only that format, never throws on malformed hashes. Client IP (src/auth/client-ip.js, FU-11): socket address by default; X-Forwarded-For is ignored unless RS_TRUST_PROXY=1, then only the last hop and only if net.isIP accepts it (IPv4-mapped IPv6 collapsed, IPv6 lower-cased), else the socket address; an invalid value never becomes a throttle key. RBAC (src/auth/rbac.js): authorize(ctx, route) for non-public routes: policy signature is allowed only for POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey (no session, no CSRF) else 403; Origin check on non-GET first; no session -> 401; role mismatch -> 403 FORBIDDEN; then X-CSRF-Token must equal the session token (403 CSRF_FAILED). Admin (src/services/users.js ensureAdmin, called from main.js): scrypt hash from RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD, disabled row with an unusable hash when unset, password change or disable ends the admin sessions, a non-admin 'admin' row stops startup. Audit (src/services/audit.js): sanitised detail (ids and codes only) for auth.signin ok/failed/denied, auth.signout, auth.register ok/failed/denied. src/app.js: builds deps.auth, default access hook is the RBAC hook, an injected authorize still replaces it (b1's test double contract unchanged), ctx gains session/sessionId/identified, clientIp moved to src/auth/client-ip.js. TESTS: test/api/auth.test.js (52 cases) and test/unit/auth/* (67 cases). Criteria to evidence: all of them by ev:ev-mv2pf62t-01198c9f (119 tests pass under the net guard; the test names start with ARCH-25, SEC-1, SEC-9, SEC-13, SEC-20, SEC-B-9, F-TR-17, RS-30, FU-6, T6); failing state before any work ev:ev-mv2p31zi-01021921; full suite npm test 509/509 and NFR5 p95 92 ms ev:ev-mv2pg2ag-0141772a. Decisions: (1) X-Forwarded-For is not trusted by default (spec default is no proxy). (2) The access hook is only called for non-public routes (b1 contract, and b1's own tests register public POST routes), so the two public POST routes check CSRF inside their handlers. (3) Rejecting validation failures before the throttle: a 422 uses no register budget and no sign-in failure row.
remainingIssues: AUTHORIZE HOOK CONTRACT for c2/c3/e-tasks: do not pass an authorize to createApp. Declare the policy on router.add: 'customer' | 'supplier' | 'admin' | 'session' (any signed-in role). The hook runs before the handler and sets ctx.user = {id, username, displayName, role, supplierId, supplierCode}, ctx.session = {idHash, csrfToken, createdAt, expiresAt}, ctx.sessionId. Anonymous 401 UNAUTHENTICATED, wrong role 403 FORBIDDEN, bad Origin or missing/wrong X-CSRF-Token on any non-GET 403 CSRF_FAILED. Scope queries by ctx.user.id (customer) or ctx.user.supplierId (supplier) in SQL. toPublicUser(user) in src/services/users.js gives the contract User object.

Public routes that need the user (PayPal return/cancel 'anonymous -> 303 to sign-in' in the RBAC matrix, per e2) must be registered with policy 'public' and call ctx.auth.identify(ctx) (returns the user or null, never throws) or ctx.auth.requireRole(ctx, ...roles) (401/403). A policy 'customer' route cannot redirect an anonymous caller. A public state-changing route gets no automatic CSRF check: it must call checkOrigin and a token check itself (see guardPreLogin in src/routes/auth.js). test/unit/auth/rbac.test.js asserts that the only public non-GET routes are POST /api/auth/register and POST /api/auth/signin, so a task that adds another will see that test fail and must decide deliberately (update the list in that test, which is owned by c1 and would need a rework or a one-line change agreed with the orchestrator).

The webhook route (e3) must be registered as POST /api/webhooks/paypal/:merchantKey with policy 'signature'; the hook skips session and CSRF for exactly that method and template and returns 403 for any other 'signature' route. Its own per-IP rate limit (60/min, 'webhook_ip') and ctx.clientIp() are the task's job.

ensureAdmin({db, config, clock}) runs in src/main.js startApp only. Tests that use test/helpers/app-harness.js do not get an admin account unless they call ensureAdmin themselves (see test/api/auth.test.js), and createApp does not provision it. The harness also does not run main.js, so no csrf_key row exists beforehand: createAuth creates it lazily with getOrCreateMeta.

The general per-user limit (300 requests/min, details.limit 'general') and the webhook/extract limits are not part of c1 and are not implemented here; rate_events kind 'general' exists in the schema. If no later task owns the general limit, the delivery lead should assign it (it would sit in the access hook after identification).

The cross-IP delay (1-10 s) uses a real timer (auth.sleep, injectable through createAuth), so API tests that exercise it take about 1 s each and pass record:false to keep NFR5 samples clean. Fixed-clock tests do not make it faster.

IPv6 clients can rotate through a /64 to get a fresh per-IP budget: the throttle key is the full address (the spec says per IP). Not changed; a /64 key would be a small change in src/auth/client-ip.js if the security reviewer wants it.
Registration reveals USERNAME_TAKEN (accepted in the spec as T24 note) and counts against the register budget, which is what limits enumeration.
Latency samples: the sign-in/register tests record their requests through the harness as usual (scrypt is about 50 ms); p95 over the whole suite was 92 ms in the full run.
The seeded RS_ADMIN_PASSWORD check is config's (>= 16 chars, placeholder refusal); ensureAdmin trusts config. The raw environment value is only held in the Secret and in the scrypt call.
nextAction: delivery-lead: dispatch the independent phase-C review of c1 (spec revision 3, Authentication, RBAC matrix, SEC-1/SEC-9/SEC-B-9/F-TR-17), then release c2-requests-plans-view with the authorize-hook contract above.

lessonDecisions.note: Its appliesWhen is a tool-call guard or hook that maps file writes to a project record or root in a multi-record repository. This task writes HTTP auth code and touches no hook, guard or root-resolution code, and I was never denied a write in the nested record.
